destination.name: Coffs Harbour
destination.tagline: A beachside holiday city two thirds of the way between Sydney and Brisbane.
destination.description: Coffs Harbour has been a family holiday stop on the east coast since the 1950s, with beaches, a marina and a developed tourist industry. The Big Banana, opened in 1964, is Australia's original Big Thing. A breakwall leads to Muttonbird Island, a nature reserve where wedge-tailed shearwaters nest, and Bongil Bongil National Park to the south has one of the largest koala populations in New South Wales. Woolgoolga to the north adds a Sikh temple and quieter beaches.
whyVisit: Look for koalas in Bongil Bongil

goodToKnow.title: Shearwaters nest from November
goodToKnow.detail: Wedge-tailed shearwaters nest on Muttonbird Island from about November; the island is steep and treeless, so bring a hat and water.

goodToKnow.title: Park Beach can be rough
goodToKnow.detail: Park Beach is the main surf beach, just north of the Coffs Creek mouth; swimming there can be rough, and the sheltered beach inside the creek mouth suits small children.

goodToKnow.title: Drive or take the coast train
goodToKnow.detail: The city is a 530 km drive north of Sydney on the Pacific Highway, with heavy traffic in peak holiday periods; NSW TrainLink also runs a daily service.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Coffs Harbour is busiest in the summer holidays, but {months} suit it well: warm beach weather, whales passing offshore into November and the shearwaters returning to Muttonbird Island in November.
